summary: Manu Goyal, founding engineer at Braintrust, opens the evals track with a personal narrative and practical argument for why evaluation matters in AI engineering. He recounts a childhood frustration with rule-based systems—symbolized by his Nintendo 64—which motivated his career in AI. After landing a job in the self-driving car industry, he observed a critical gap: improving model metrics (e.g., image classification from 98% to 99%) is necessary but insufficient for production deployment. Real-world questions—does the system avoid pedestrians, negotiate traffic, obey the law—require contextual evaluation, not just accuracy improvements. Goyal frames evals as more than unit tests or regression detectors. Without evals, the only feedback signal comes from shipping to production, which is expensive, slow, and risky. Investing in good evals creates a laboratory for experimentation, enabling teams to complete roughly 90% of the product iteration loop before production, allowing faster and more confident shipping. Furthermore, applying the same evaluation metrics to online production data yields data-driven signals about which examples are most useful for the next iteration, creating a continuous improvement cycle. He cites tech luminaries—including Kevin While, Gary Tan, Mike Kger, and Greg Brockman—as endorsing the necessity of evals, suggesting broad industry consensus. At Braintrust, the goal is to build a developer platform encompassing evals, prompt tweaking, playground experimentation, data logging, observability, and a data flywheel connecting these components. Goyal distills the talk to one message: the key to industry transformation and success is evals. He directs attendees to the eval track in Golden Gate Ballroom B.

sections.summary: Manu Goyal introduces himself as a founding engineer at Braintrust. He shares a childhood photo playing Nintendo 64, framing it as disappointment with rule-based technology and motivation for an AI career.

sections.title: Lessons from Self-Driving Cars
sections.summary: Goyal recounts working in self-driving cars, where he learned that tuning models and improving accuracy metrics is insufficient for production. Real-world evaluation of pedestrian avoidance, traffic negotiation, and legal compliance is essential.

sections.title: The Value of Evals Beyond Unit Tests
sections.summary: Evals are framed as more than unit tests or regression detectors. Without evals, feedback comes only from production—expensive, slow, and risky. Good evals create a laboratory enabling roughly 90% of iteration before production. Applying consistent metrics offline and online creates data-driven signals for next iterations.

sections.title: Industry Endorsement and Braintrust Platform
